preamble: Solutions to 13 clues include sequences of letters of varying lengths not indicated in the wordplay. These sequences are all of a kind.

solutions.check: grid and clues read from the Guardian's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Turning head, see about top issue

indicators.note: the head of a word is its front, so turning it flips round the opening pair of letters
about means going around, so the word see wraps the word for top

parts.note: taken as the verb, see stays as written
a cap is a top, as on a bottle or pen

explanation.surface: A publisher, looking round, sees to the lead story of the next edition.
explanation.walkthrough: The see here is the verb, not a bishop's seat. 'Turning head' swaps the front pair of letters of the wrapped result, SECAPE. One of the few entries here with no hidden capital.
explanation.definitionFit: As nouns, an issue and an escape both mean an outflow, a way of getting out, as water issues from a leak.

clue.text: Sort of acid (blah, blah, blah)

parts.note: etc. stands for the rest of the tedious list, like blah blah blah
one of the capital cities the preamble hides, unclued: the capital of Vietnam

explanation.surface: Someone droning on and on about a particular acid.
explanation.walkthrough: The preamble's thirteen unclued sequences are all capital cities; one of them is tucked inside this entry, with nothing in the clue for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethanoic acid is the chemist's name for acetic acid, the sharp component of vinegar.

clue.text: Day visiting Greek island? They'll likely be drawn

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside a place, so one word is put within the other

parts.note: Cos (Kos) is an island in the Dodecanese
Mon is the abbreviation for Monday
an unclued capital city, as the preamble says: the capital of France

explanation.surface: A day-tripper's trip to a Greek island invites inevitable comparisons with home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawn' suggests pictures of the island; comparisons are drawn in the sense of made.
explanation.definitionFit: People commonly draw comparisons between two things, so comparisons are what is drawn.

clue.text: Way to waste time that is contemptible!

indicators.note: to waste something is to lose or throw it away, so that letter goes

parts.note: a path is a way
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone sneering at a pastime as an idle waste of hours.
explanation.definitionFit: Pah is an exclamation of scorn, the noise someone makes on finding a thing beneath them.

clue.text: Good, Devon and Cornwall overturned action

parts.note: the hidden sequence the preamble leaves unclued: Oslo, capital of Norway

indicators.note: overturned means flipped over, so the letters for the region run backwards

parts.note: Devon and Cornwall are the counties of England's South West, abbreviated SW

explanation.surface: Something good happened in the West Country, then everything was turned upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: Per the preamble, a capital city (OSLO, Norway's) is slipped in without wordplay; 'overturned' turns SW into WS. Devon and Cornwall are counties in the far south-west of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Go-slows are a form of industrial action, where workers deliberately work slowly as a protest.

clue.text: Architectural feature's old, very old, look!

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old
V is the abbreviation for very
O for old again, then lo, an old word for look

explanation.surface: A guide pointing out an ancient piece of a building with excitement.
explanation.definitionFit: An ovolo is a convex moulding, roughly a quarter-circle in section, used in classical buildings.

clue.text: American's apparently neutral deity

indicators.note: what is apparent is plainly visible, here sitting in plain view inside the next word

parts.note: the closing letters of the word, read upwards in this down entry

explanation.surface: An American god who seems to take no side.
explanation.walkthrough: No word signals the turnaround; in a down entry the letters simply read upwards from the end of the word. The role of 'American’s' is unclear and it is treated here as padding.
explanation.definitionFit: A lar was a Roman household god, one of the lares who guarded the family home.

clue.text: Greer's kind in pool not making either end?

indicators.note: failing to reach either end means the first and last letters are dropped

parts.note: someone in a pool is swimming

explanation.surface: A question whether feminist Germaine Greer's sort of people, swimming in a pool, can't reach either side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not making either end' drops the outer letters. Germaine Greer is an Australian feminist writer; her 'kind' is women, here in the deliberate feminist respelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Wimmin is a feminist spelling of women avoiding the word man, associated with 1970s-80s feminism such as Greer's.

clue.text: Calculating pair admitting love, opening whisky dispenser

indicators.note: opening here means the combined piece splits the dispenser apart and sits inside it

parts.note: an optic is the measuring device fixed to an upturned bottle behind a bar

indicators.note: admitting means the pair's letters let love in between them

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O
the unclued themed sequence: Tunis is the capital of Tunisia

explanation.surface: A scheming couple, letting a lover in, starts up the bar's whisky optic.
explanation.walkthrough: The preamble's unclued sequences are all capital cities; here the one of Tunisia joins the wordplay with no signal. 'Whisky dispenser' sounds like a person but is the bar fitting.
explanation.definitionFit: An opportunistic person is calculating, exploiting chances for self-interest without scruple.

clue.text: Women on stage overdoing hoax savage in act

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for women
to ham is to overact
bam is an old word for a hoax or trick

explanation.surface: A comic turn in which actresses overplay a practical joke with violence.
explanation.definitionFit: Wham-bam describes something abrupt and forceful, as in a hasty, rough act of sex.

clue.text: Circus in school

parts.note: in, meaning fashionable, is hip
a school of whales or dolphins is also called a pod
the hidden sequence the preamble leaves unclued: Rome, capital of Italy

explanation.surface: A circus is staged within a school.
explanation.walkthrough: Per the preamble, ROME (Italy's capital) is added without wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A hippodrome was an ancient arena for horse and chariot races, and the name is used for circus and variety theatres.

clue.text: Old ruler conspiring with night owl cries off

indicators.note: these noises are taken off, removed from the end of the phrase

parts.note: in cahoots means conspiring together
owls hoot at night

explanation.surface: An ancient king plotting, with the owls' calls cancelled for the night.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inca was the emperor of the Andean empire conquered by Spain in the sixteenth century.

clue.text: Thick-skinned types take in hot drink

indicators.note: in means the letter for take goes inside the drink's letters

parts.note: cocoa is a hot chocolate drink
R stands for recipe, Latin for take, as written at the head of prescriptions
the unclued themed sequence DILI (capital of East Timor) is slipped in before the final A

explanation.surface: Some insensitive people grab a hot drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Per the preamble, DILI, the capital of East Timor, appears without wordplay; it sits between COCO and A once R has gone into COCOA after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Crocodilia is the order of reptiles with armoured hides, so its members are literally thick-skinned animals.

clue.text: $100 on head of sex god's a sizeable wedge

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100
a hunk is a muscular, attractive man

explanation.surface: A hundred dollars staked on a heartthrob makes a decent wad of cash.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, C on the head of HUNK sits above it.
explanation.definitionFit: A chunk is a thick, substantial piece of something, like a solid wedge of cheese.

clue.text: "Part of Campania" is sign over football club on day of pranks

parts.note: taken as written
Leo is a sign of the zodiac
FC is the abbreviation for football club
April Fools' Day is APR 1, the 1 written as I

explanation.surface: A star sign hanging over a football club's April Fools' stunt in southern Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: The date April 1 is written APR 1, with the digit read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Capri is an island in the Bay of Naples, which lies in the Italian region of Campania.

clue.text: Admitted to "retro" University, one's exhibiting cunning with wickedness

indicators.note: retro means backwards-looking, so University and one are taken in reverse order from how the clue lists them

parts.note: someone admitted to a place is in
the Roman numeral I is one
the hidden sequence the preamble leaves unclued: Quito, capital of Ecuador
cunning means sly

explanation.surface: A student taken into an old-fashioned university is clever and wicked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retro' puts one (I) ahead of University (U), and QUITO (Ecuador's capital, unclued per the preamble) sits between those two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Iniquity is wickedness, so acting iniquitously is behaving in a wicked, grossly unjust manner.

clue.text: Withdraw organisation with HQ in New York, perhaps

parts.words: organisation with HQ in New York
parts.note: the United Nations has its headquarters in New York
say means for example, as perhaps does

explanation.surface: A body based in Manhattan might pull out.
explanation.definitionFit: To unsay something is to take back or retract a statement you have made.

clue.text: What lifts non-Christians?

parts.note: helium, chemical symbol He, is the gas that lifts balloons and airships
the hidden sequence the preamble leaves unclued: Athens, capital of Greece

explanation.surface: A question about what raises the spirits of unbelievers.
explanation.walkthrough: Per the preamble, ATHENS (Greece's capital) is added without wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Heathens are people who do not follow a major religion, traditionally from a Christian standpoint, i.e. pagans.

clue.text: Commander cracks on the subject of something finely poised

indicators.note: cracks means the commander and the theme letters break into the word for about, splitting it open

parts.note: RE is the Latin-derived word for regarding or about
OC is the military abbreviation for Officer Commanding
the unclued themed sequence: Kingston is the capital of Jamaica

explanation.surface: A commanding officer breaks down while discussing something delicately balanced.
explanation.walkthrough: The preamble's unclued sequences are all capital cities; here Jamaica's capital rides in alongside the commander with no signal of its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A rocking stone is a large boulder balanced so delicately that a push makes it sway without toppling.

clue.text: Gold stars …

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
the hidden sequence the preamble leaves unclued: Riga, capital of Latvia

explanation.surface: Gold stars awarded, the ellipsis carrying on into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: Per the preamble, RIGA (Latvia's capital) is added without wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Auriga, the Charioteer, is a northern constellation, a named group of stars including Capella.

clue.text: Perhaps SPECTRE agent is an oddball, wearing dodgy syrups

indicators.note: one piece wears the other, which therefore sits inside it like clothing
an oddball is out of the ordinary, so these words come out in an odd order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something dodgy is unreliable and not straight, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Bond villain's eccentric henchman sporting a cheap wig.
explanation.walkthrough: Syrup is rhyming slang for a wig (syrup of figs), which shapes the surface. SPECTRE is the villains' organisation in the James Bond stories.
explanation.definitionFit: A Soviet agent is one example of a SPECTRE operative, as with Rosa Klebb in From Russia with Love.

clue.text: … for separating an area, of course

indicators.note: a thing that separates two letters stands between them

parts.note: taken as written
pro means for, in favour of

explanation.surface: Something that keeps one area apart from another, as you might expect.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this to the previous clue, but each clue stands alone. 'Of course' is not the throwaway phrase it seems; it means on a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: On a golf course the apron is the closely mown fringe around the green.

clue.text: Business centre revolutionised by ticking boxes

indicators.note: a revolution turns things round, so the letters run backwards
to box is to enclose, so the words that follow hold the letters

parts.note: the letters run across the gap between the two words

explanation.surface: A financial district transformed by form-filling bureaucrats.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district, the Square Mile.
explanation.definitionFit: The City, or a city's financial quarter, is where banks and businesses are concentrated.

clue.text: Prison sentence's upper limit

parts.note: doing time is serving a prison sentence
an unclued capital city, as the preamble says: the capital of Germany

explanation.surface: A judge's sentence that reaches the maximum allowed.
explanation.definitionFit: The timberline is the altitude above which trees cannot grow on a mountain, the highest boundary of forest.

clue.text: See 9
The taxman's covering letter

indicators.note: the outer words cover and conceal what lies inside them

parts.note: the letters straddle the two words

explanation.surface: A tax inspector sending a cover letter with the demand.
explanation.definitionFit: Eta is the seventh character of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Leak: phosphorus beginning to appear

parts.note: to take a leak is slang for to pee
P is the chemical symbol for phosphorus

explanation.surface: A chemistry lab where a phosphorus spill starts to show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leak' looks like an escape of liquid; it is slang for urinating.
explanation.definitionFit: To peep is to start to emerge, showing just a little, as the sun peeps out from cloud.

clue.text: Attempt to evacuate corrupt politicians

indicators.note: evacuating a word empties out its inside, so only the first and last letters of the attempt stay

parts.note: an attempt is a try
the hidden sequence the preamble leaves unclued: Amman, capital of Jordan

explanation.surface: An effort to clear out a crooked political gang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to evacuate' empties TRY to TY, and AMMAN (Jordan's capital, unclued per the preamble) fills the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: Tammany Hall was the New York Democratic Party machine notorious for graft, so its name stands for corrupt politics.

clue.text: Order something that's silvery-white on the table

parts.words: something that's silvery-white on the table
parts.note: caesium, symbol Cs, is a silvery-white metal in the periodic table
an unclued capital city, as the preamble says: the capital of Samoa

explanation.surface: Asking for the silver to be laid on the dining table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The table' looks like dinner but is the periodic table.
explanation.definitionFit: A capias is a legal writ ordering an officer to arrest a named person.
